**Yield:** one 9 x 13-inch pan · **Cook:** 30 min

## Ingredients

- 4 tablespoons butter, plus more for the mushrooms
- 1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
- 3 to 4 stalks celery, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1 container mushrooms
- salt and pepper
- 1 pound sausage, at the most
- 1 package peeled, partially cooked chestnuts
- 1 bag (12 ounces) Pepperidge Farm seasoned stuffing
- about 2 ½ cups turkey stock, plus extra

## Method

1. Sauté the onion, garlic and celery in the butter.
2. Sauté the mushrooms lightly in more butter. They take up butter quickly. Salt and pepper them well.
3. In another pan, sauté the sausage, breaking it up as it cooks. Drain off the fat.
4. Break the chestnuts into pieces.
5. Stir the mushrooms, the sausage and the chestnuts into the vegetables, then stir in the stuffing.
6. Add stock a little at a time until it is as moist as you want. A little on the dry side is good.
7. Bake it in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan, covered, at 350°F for 30 minutes, until hot. Or stuff a bird with it.

## Notes

- My mom's recipe. The onion, celery, sausage and mushrooms are her amounts for a small batch; the rest are sized for one bag of stuffing.
- The mushrooms give the stuffing a nice earthiness, but they do not taste of much unless they are well seasoned.
- Peeled, partially cooked chestnuts are sold at good food stores, which saves roasting and shelling them.
- The pan, oven temperature, time and the amount of stock for one bag are from Pepperidge Farm's [Moist & Savory Stuffing](https://www.pepperidgefarm.com/recipe/moist-savory-stuffing/) (read 2026-11-16), which also says to bake it uncovered for a crunchier top.
- It is my mom's take on my [grandmother's stuffing](grandmother-s-stuffing.md).
